proposition: all vectors forming the embeddings, MLP, attention matrices and hidden states are unit norm normalized.
notes: Intentionally scoped to the paper's explicit abstract statement; this record does not claim a causal explanation for nGPT performance.

proposition: The paper characterizes bisimulation-preserving linear quotient maps for finite-dimensional linear control systems under its specified observation and timing semantics.
notes: No arbitrary nonlinear quotient or unrestricted observation-map converse. Corrects the provisional domain-scaling-lab DOI 10.1016/S0005-1098(03)00255-3; that identifier was never accepted here.

proposition: The Isabelle development proves both directions of Myhill–Nerode using regular expressions; its combined theorem fixes a finite alphabet.
notes: Manuel Eberl is credited as a contributor. Source inspection is not an independent Isabelle build, nor proof of a general observation-quotient adapter.

proposition: For a finite parameter tuple, the paper establishes finite-outcome decision-comparison/garbling equivalence and extends comparisons beyond finite outcomes through its standard-measure formulation.
notes: Preserve the Borel-field setup, closed bounded convex loss-vector sets, and state-independent kernel. Theorem 8 concerns auxiliary bounded standard-measure supports. No unrestricted general-state converse is imported.

proposition: For a bounded matrix family, arbitrary-switching asymptotic stability is characterized by joint spectral radius below one.
notes: Definitions 1.1–1.2 concern asymptotic product growth. This does not make per-step singular extrema sharp iff tests; stabilizability concerns a vanishing product operator norm, not merely one initial vector.

proposition: The lower-spectral-radius algorithm has a convergence theorem for restricted finite real asymptotically rank-one families with the specified invariant-cone and antinorm hypotheses.
notes: Every nonempty product must be asymptotically rank-one. Require proper invariant K, K intersect closure(H(F)) = {0}, and positive antinorm; bound gap tends to selected delta > 0. No unrestricted computability conclusion.

proposition: Operator Schmidt rank equals the ordinary matrix rank of realignment for the specified finite-dimensional bipartite tensor decomposition.
notes: The preprint title is Restrictions on the Schmidt rank of bipartite unitary operators beyond dimension two. Do not extend this identity to arbitrary multipartite tensor rank.

proposition: A Hausdorff countable-atlas C^r m-manifold without boundary, r at least one (including smooth), is C^r-equivalent to an analytic manifold in Euclidean dimension 2m+1.
notes: The weak embedding bound does not require compactness. The 2m result with regular singularities in theorem 3 is not the strong embedding theorem. No distortion, isometry, dimension optimality or boundary extension is asserted.

proposition: Every positive-dimensional smooth manifold without boundary, under the usual Hausdorff and countable-atlas conventions, admits an embedding in Euclidean dimension twice its manifold dimension.
notes: The original paper calls C^1 regular maps smooth. Preserve that historical regularity convention when citing its proof. The positive-dimension qualification is necessary: the proof treats dimensions 1, 2 and then at least 3; a multi-point zero-dimensional manifold cannot inject into R^0. No compactness, connectedness or orientability premise is needed. This is an existence bound, not a generic 2m projection, chord-metric preservation, distortion bound or minimal dimension claim.

proposition: On a compact m-manifold, a generic pair consisting of a C^2 diffeomorphism and a C^2 scalar observation yields a delay-coordinate embedding into R^(2m+1), using iterates zero through 2m.
notes: Genericity is over the pair, not a guarantee for an arbitrary fixed dynamics or observation. Do not substitute attractor dimension for manifold dimension, infer arbitrary sampling guarantees, or conclude metric preservation, noise robustness, finite-data learnability or generalization.

proposition: For 0 < tau < 1, an n-point (n at least two) Euclidean configuration admits a map to dimension floor(K(tau) Log n) with the product of forward and inverse Lipschitz constants at most (1+tau)/(1-tau); K(tau) may be chosen of order tau^(-2).
notes: Lemma 1 uses a subset of l_2^n; an arbitrary finite Euclidean configuration fits its affine span. The proof takes K at least (10/tau)^2. The familiar O(epsilon^(-2) log n) approximate-distance formulation follows by parameter adjustment and rescaling. This concerns finite Euclidean sets, not infinite domains, exact isometry, arbitrary non-Euclidean metrics or every projection. The paper defines Log n as max(1, natural log n). The proof uses a rank-k orthogonal projection with positive probability, so a rescaled linear map suffices. Empty and singleton configurations are trivial separate cases.

proposition: Under the manuscript definitions of Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifolds without boundary and smooth meaning C-infinity, the positive-dimensional strong Whitney theorem gives a smooth embedding into twice the manifold dimension.
notes: This is a versioned manuscript statement attributed to Whitney, not a full proof. The draft display omits n>0; retain the positive-dimensional restriction because the multi-point zero-dimensional counterexample invalidates an unrestricted reading. Source identity/version are internal and corroborated by the institutional course page; the mirror is not author-hosted. Assign no published-edition DOI or theorem numbering. April 2001 corrections in another bundle do not date this December 2000 draft. No metric-preservation claim.

proposition: Standard positive-dimensional smooth Riemannian manifolds without boundary with positive C^k metrics, 3≤k≤infinity, admit C^k isometric embeddings into sufficiently high finite-dimensional Euclidean space; the paper treats both compact and noncompact cases.
notes: Isometry means the induced Riemannian metric, hence preservation of tangent inner products and curve lengths/intrinsic distances within the image, not equality of intrinsic distance to ambient Euclidean chord distance. Completeness is unnecessary. The 1956 theorem includes C-infinity but does not assert the C2 or analytic result; the separate C1 theory is not being substituted. No arbitrary metric-space embedding, arbitrary projection or efficient learned architecture follows.

proposition: A C1 one-form on a star-shaped open subset of R^n whose coefficient derivatives are symmetric equals df for a C2 real function on that domain. Under the Euclidean vector/covector identification this is the gradient-potential converse.
notes: On arbitrary open sets this supplies local potentials through small balls. A global potential on a general connected open domain instead requires every closed piecewise-smooth path integral to vanish. Holes permit counterexamples; they do not force every closed field to be non-exact. A potential alone implies neither discrete-step descent nor training success. Author metadata confirms version/date/ISBN; no DOI is asserted.

proposition: For a real d-dimensional vector space and 0≤k≤d, graph charts for k-planes transverse to a fixed complementary subspace define a Hausdorff second-countable C-infinity manifold without boundary of dimension k(d-k). Chart overlaps are open and transition maps are smooth.
notes: For old-to-new block coordinates (x,y) ↦ (a x+b y,c x+d y), equation 1.2 translates to A ↦ (c+dA)(a+bA)^(-1) on the invertible-overlap domain. This block notation is a faithful translation, not a verbatim displayed formula. Real finite-dimensional Grassmannian; no complex or infinite-dimensional extension. Reuses the already identified December 2000 manuscript work, with no published-edition DOI.

proposition: For real Grassmann manifolds with the standard positive-definite inner product, orthogonal complementation is a C-infinity diffeomorphism from G(k,d) to G(d-k,d).
notes: The complement diffeomorphism is stated explicitly within the tangent/vector-bundle construction rather than as a separately numbered proof. Do not extend it to arbitrary choices of complement, indefinite orthogonality or a complex-holomorphic complement map.

proposition: For two subspaces of a finite-dimensional real or complex positive-definite inner-product space, simultaneous orthogonal complementation preserves the principal-angle lists after adding zero entries to match lengths. The singular values of the difference of their orthogonal projectors are the duplicated sines of those angles together with abs(dim X-dim Y) additional ones, with zero padding on either side as needed.
notes: Theorem 2.7 equation (2.3) and Theorem 2.9 do not assume equal subspace dimensions. Principal-angle lists have min(dim X,dim Y) entries; they need not retain length after complementation. Equal ranks remove the rank-difference extra ones, not the doubled ones from right angles. Empty-angle maximum needs a separate convention. No indefinite metric, oblique projector or unrestricted infinite-dimensional conclusion.

proposition: In the positive-sheet n-dimensional real hyperbolic-space model of curvature scale a>0, geodesic polar radius r gives metric dr²+(sinh(a r)/a)² dΩ² and angularly integrated radial volume element Vol(S^(n−1)) (sinh(a r)/a)^(n−1) dr.
notes: Equations (6.2)–(6.3) and the following paragraph on printed p.644 supply the geodesic coordinate, metric and density. R=-n(n−1)a² is scalar curvature, as defined on p.638; sectional curvature is -a². The positive origin x0=1/a in the positive-sheet model supplies a>0. Positive exponential growth requires n>=2; that dimension qualification is a consequence of the formula, not an extra quoted assertion. For n=1 the density is constant and ball volume is linear. No general variable-negative-curvature comparison, packing existence, tree embedding or architectural/generalization claim is imported.

proposition: For an open subset U of finite-dimensional Euclidean space R^n, every continuous injection U -> R^n has open image (invariance of domain).
notes: Theorem 2B.3, printed p.172. No connectedness, compactness, differentiability or nonemptiness is needed for the theorem itself; n=0 is trivially valid. The lower-target-dimension consequence requires a nonempty source and is a separate project adapter using inclusion into a proper linear subspace. The domain is open in Euclidean space; boundary half-charts and arbitrary subsets do not satisfy this hypothesis. Corollary 2B.4 is not separately imported: its compact-source/connected-target surjectivity claim requires nonempty source, omitted in the displayed statement.
